detail.rainNote: Rain is the weather model's estimate, adjusted upward (more at altitude) to match rain gauges; forecast days have no such adjustment.
detail.terrainNote: Temperatures and drying are adjusted to this cell's slope: slopes that get more sun than flat ground are warmer and dry out faster, shadier ones are cooler.

disclaimer.title: Conditions only, never edibility
disclaimer.body1: Mappa Funghi estimates whether the weather and woodland favour porcini, ovoli and gallinacci fruiting. It doesn't say where mushrooms are, doesn't identify them, and never says whether a mushroom is safe to eat.
disclaimer.body2: The conditions score runs from 0 to 1 and is not a probability. More than a few days ahead it is a trend, not a certainty.
disclaimer.body3: Before eating any mushroom you pick, have it checked for free by your local ASL mycological inspectorate.
disclaimer.short: Conditions only: Mappa Funghi doesn't identify mushrooms or judge whether they are edible.

credits.title: Data and credits

outlook.title: Outlook
outlook.subtitle: {{species}} · {{area}}
outlook.pickSpecies: The outlook covers one species at a time. Pick one:
outlook.soFarNote: From {{start}} to {{end}}; observed weather up to {{weather}}.
outlook.outOfSeason: Nothing to look ahead to: the {{species}} season runs {{window}}.
outlook.how1: For each period we count in how many past seasons ({{years}}) at least {{share}} of the area's woodland had good days on the same dates. It is a count, not a probability.
outlook.how2: The mark follows the rain before the period: {{species}} respond to rain {{min}}–{{max}} days earlier. From {{wetter}} of normal up the period reads better than usual, from {{drier}} down worse.
outlook.how3: For past days and the next 7 we use observed and forecast weather; beyond that, ECMWF's long-range tendencies, which only say whether an area will be wetter or drier than normal.
outlook.leadRain: Rain in the days before: {{percent}} of normal
